messages.subject: nlminb and nlminb.constr
parts:
Hello, I'm trying to understand how the optimization algorithm works for a cfa model. 
I can see that when the model syntax does not include any "==", ">" or "<" operators, the default optimized is "nlminb", and only when the model syntax includes any "==", ">" or "<" operators the "nlminb.constr" is used. Since the confirmatory setting "constrains" some loadings to be equal to zero and not to be estimated, how is this gauranted when using the simple  "nlminb" option?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: nlminb and nlminb.constr
parts: Since the confirmatory setting "constrains" some loadings to be equal to zero and not to be estimated, how is this gauranted when using the simple  "nlminb" option?

Constraining estimated parameters is not the same as fixing parameters (which is constraining to a specific value, not to be the same as another value or limiting the estimate's range).  Fixed parameters do not need the additional complexity of nlminb.constr

Terrence D. Jorgensen
